title: Kadala Curry
description: Black chickpeas simmered in a roasted coconut-and-spice gravy — a hearty Kerala breakfast side, classically paired with puttu or appam.
steps: Pressure cook the soaked black chickpeas with the water and 1 tsp of the salt for 5-6 whistles until soft. Set aside, reserving the cooking liquid.

Dry roast the grated coconut, coriander seeds and dried red chillies in a pan over low heat until the coconut turns golden brown and fragrant. Cool slightly, then grind with the roughly chopped onion and a splash of water into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter, then add the curry leaves.
Add the ginger garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add the chopped tomato and turmeric, cooking until the tomato softens.
Add the ground coconut-onion paste and cook for 5-6 minutes, stirring often, until the raw smell is gone and the mixture darkens slightly.

Add the cooked chickpeas along with their reserved cooking liquid, the remaining salt and garam masala. Simmer for 10-12 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
Serve hot with puttu, appam or idiyappam.
